title: Leotha's reaction and why he had to leave Charleston
summary: He explains that he knew music had to come from New York, though his wife did not want him to go.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How was it with Leota? Was she satisfied?
Did she really not want you to be a musician?
No, I don't think so. I don't think she felt that she didn't want me to be a musician.
No, she didn't want like me going away.
The other thing was, you know, I mean, you have a family. You've got to provide, don't you?
Yes. Right. Well, you know, I had to send money back, like you say.

Well, I mean, whatever I was wondering was when you decided you could make it as a musician. You know, that must have been quite a decision to take. When you have to provide for this family out of playing the banjo or the guitar.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm. Yeah. I know. Well, I figured, if I could get away -- I knew I wouldn't be able to make it in Charleston, -- not playing music. Not, you know.
I had to get away. And, because of the fact I had been to New York --
You see -- I had been there, and I had seen, and I had heard, and I knew whatever had to come -- it had to come from New York.
So, I knew how she felt about it, you know, but I had to get away, and then eventually --
She didn't really want to leave Charleston, I guess?
No. Because under the conditions I wouldn't want her to leave. And I, you know --
I had to go, but on a thing like that --
-- to provide for your family. Helen wanted to know -- did she want to go to New York?
